clue.text: Bird attacked bird

parts.note: to have bitten someone is to have attacked them with the teeth
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: One bird has gone for another in a squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: The bittern is a wading bird of the heron family, known for its booming call.

clue.text: Account in newspaper subsequently in need of clarification

parts.note: i is a British national daily newspaper

indicators.note: the account abbreviation goes inside the other letters

parts.note: subsequently means next, afterwards

explanation.surface: A newspaper report that will need clearing up later.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British daily paper, so the newspaper gives just the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imprecise or vague still needs to be made clearer, a fair synonym.

clue.text: Issue getting helmet on head of cyclist

parts.note: a topi is a sun helmet, the pith helmet of the colonial era

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so take only the start of cyclist

explanation.surface: A question of whether riders must wear helmets.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' says the helmet sits above the cyclist's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue under discussion is a subject or theme, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Concerned with educational institution on French island

parts.note: re means about, concerning, as in a letter heading
uni is short for university

explanation.surface: Someone worried about a college located on a French island.
explanation.definitionFit: La Réunion is an island in the Indian Ocean that is an overseas department of France.

clue.text: Son with right punching old man, naturally prickly?

indicators.note: the right letter punches its way into the husband word, ending up inside it

parts.note: one's old man is one's husband, informally hubby

explanation.surface: A boy and his right hook, hitting his dad, who is naturally touchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prickly' looks like a temper; the question mark warns it means covered in bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground thick with bushes is full of thorny growth, so prickly by nature, a playful sense.

clue.text: I'm being introduced to contemporary music containing minimum of harmony — this?

definitions.text: I'm being introduced to contemporary music containing minimum of harmony — this?

parts.note: hi is what a person says when introduced to someone

indicators.note: the pop letters hold the harmony letter within them

parts.note: pop is contemporary popular music

indicators.note: the least of a word is just its first letter, so take the start of harmony

explanation.surface: A newcomer to modern music asks whether a style short on harmony is the one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the genre: modern music with very little harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: This rap-based style is contemporary music built on beats and rhymes rather than harmony.

clue.text: Still messy, McCarthyite aunt's grounds for divorce?

definitions.meaning: not yet tidied away, still in a mess
a McCarthyite would divorce a husband who turned out to be a communist

explanation.surface: A messy divorce where a communist-hunting woman leaves her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Senator McCarthy hunted communists, called reds, in 1950s America.
explanation.definitionFit: A table or room not yet tidied is still in a mess, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Native American in nick after capsizing vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue capsizing turns the whole assembly upside down, so it reads from the bottom
the people's name goes into the word for nick

parts.note: to nick someone is to arrest them, to nab them
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A Native American locked up after overturning a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, but here it is a drinks container.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinks tin is a vessel in the sense of a container for liquid.

clue.text: Kilogramme awfully cheap then, gee: you deserve more!

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for kilogram

indicators.note: awfully says these letters are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone shocked at how cheap a kilo is, then praising the seller.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving away the leftover money is a tip, an idiom for telling a server they earned extra.

clue.text: Mortgage's ending, better rate coming back? That's a long, long way off

indicators.note: coming back says the whole string runs from right to left
a word's ending is its final letter, so take the end of mortgage

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it
speed is a rate of motion

explanation.surface: A borrower wonders whether a better interest rate is returning, still far off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better rate' reads as one finance phrase but is two pieces; 'coming back' turns the whole string, ECAPSPEED, round.
explanation.definitionFit: The far reaches of the universe beyond the solar system are about as remote as anywhere gets.

clue.text: An irritation voiced when checking out matinee hit, cryptically?

definitions.text: An irritation voiced when checking out

wordplay.reading: UNEXPECTED + ITEM IN THE + BAGGING + AREA

parts.note: take ... as anagram fodder, with ... as the indicator: the letters make matinee hit

explanation.surface: The supermarket self-checkout complaint, linked to a hit afternoon show.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, makes the clue words. A is the abbreviation for area.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-service tills in British shops famously announce this phrase, which shoppers find maddening.

clue.text: Discipline of the Chinese discussing what they drink in the east with Spooner?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two drink words change places

parts.note: chai is the word for tea across much of Asia
tea is the drink in question

explanation.surface: Talking about Chinese martial arts and tea-drinking with an Oxford don.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discussing' signals that the swap is of sounds: CHAI TEA spoken with starts exchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: This slow-moving Chinese martial art is practised as a discipline of exercise and meditation.

clue.text: Something flowing in Italy when quaffing wine, case of classic Italian tipple

indicators.note: quaffing means drinking down, so the river swallows the wine and the outer letters

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
rosé is pink wine

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer letters, so take the first and last of classic

explanation.surface: An Italian scene of wine flowing and classic local drink being knocked back.
explanation.definitionFit: This sparkling white wine from the Veneto is Italy's best-known fizz.

clue.text: See 11
Girl combo composed series of short messages

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A girl band wrote a run of songs or notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A platform for brief posts, such as a feed of tweets, is a stream of short messages.

clue.text: Laborious routine in stadium mentioned by royal?

indicators.note: the clipped vowels of a very posh royal accent turn the stadium word into something else when spoken

parts.note: a sports ground is a stadium

explanation.surface: A royal remarking on the tedium of a day at the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the cut-glass upper-class accent, in which the stadium word comes out with a different vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard, dull, repetitive work is a slog, a synonym in everyday speech.

clue.text: See 10
A skirt lifted, inside which an old instrument

indicators.note: the pair, once turned, holds the remaining letters inside it
in a down clue lifted reads the pair upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a skirt is an edge or border, as is a lip

explanation.surface: Something hidden beneath a raised skirt, an antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like clothing but means an edge; turned up, A LIP gives PILA.
explanation.definitionFit: A player piano, worked by perforated rolls, is a keyboard instrument.

clue.text: Possible result when charges withdrawn, having saved foundation

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it inside, so the turned word holds the other
withdrawn here means drawn back, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: people in one's care are one's wards or charges
the core of something is its basis

explanation.surface: A court case result when charges are dropped and the case kept standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charges withdrawn' sounds legal; it is WARDS turned round. A score draw is a football match drawn with goals, as on the football pools.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn football match with goals scored is one outcome among win, loss and draw.

clue.text: Intense sorrow in Constantine's Rome revved up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters read from bottom to top
in says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Grief in imperial Rome under Constantine, being stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revved up' looks like one phrase, but 'revved' gives its first letter to the run and 'up' is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep regret for wrongdoing is a painful guilty sorrow, a close synonym.

clue.text: Endless trouble breaking loose around a plant

indicators.note: the shortened phrase goes around the single letter
endless says the phrase loses its final letter

parts.note: when trouble breaks loose, all hell breaks loose: the idiom

explanation.surface: Endless trouble erupting around something.
explanation.walkthrough: From the idiom 'all hell breaks loose', the clue's 'trouble breaking loose' is ALL HELL; endless leaves ALLHEL, which goes around A.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for several herbs, such as valerian, once thought to cure all ills.

clue.text: Boy, that's labyrinthine!

definitions.meaning: something mazelike: a network of rabbit burrows, or crowded twisting streets

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at how mazelike something is.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit colony's tunnels form a maze, so the word also names any confusing tangle of passages.

clue.text: Land covering periphery of our view

indicators.note: the country wraps around the letters it covers

parts.note: Panama is a country in Central America

indicators.note: the periphery is the outside, so take the first and last letters of our

explanation.surface: Land stretching to the edge of what we can see.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide sweeping vista of a landscape is a full view in every direction.

clue.text: Chap originally captivated by savage, a bit of a looker

indicators.note: captivated means held captive, so the letter is held inside the savage word

parts.note: to savage is to maul

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so take the first letter of Chap

explanation.surface: A man first charmed by a wild one who is a bit of a looker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of a looker' sounds like an attractive person; it is part of an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow spot of the retina is a small area of the eye, the part of a looker meant.

clue.text: American mammal: film one

parts.note: a film is a thin layer or coat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A wildlife documentary featuring a single American animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' suggests cinema; it is a thin layer.
explanation.definitionFit: This raccoon relative with a long snout lives in the Americas.

clue.text: Sign of criminal activity duly noted by party

parts.note: a jolly is a party or jaunt
roger is radio talk for message received and understood

explanation.surface: A political party's misconduct has been logged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' means next to, putting the party word beside the radio word.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull-and-crossbones flag flown by pirates signals piracy, a crime at sea.

clue.text: See 11
See 11
I didn't, I didn't, Stormy Daniels!

indicators.note: stormy means turbulent, so the letters are tossed about

explanation.surface: Someone repeatedly protesting innocence about the adult film star Stormy Daniels.
explanation.walkthrough: Stormy Daniels's affair claim against Donald Trump drew repeated denials; 'Stormy' is the indicator, not part of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Each 'I didn't' is a refusal to admit something, so several make a set of repudiations.
